page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server configuration powered by Intel x86_64 processors. The instance provides direct hardware access across 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated virtual CPUs operating at up to 3.9 GHz, paired with 1536.0 GB of system memory. Operating without virtualization layer overhead, it offers a consistent 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core along with a 200 Gbps baseline network interface.

Storage resources include 11,400 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage. While the system does not incorporate GPU acceleration, the density of physical compute cores combined with massive memory and fast ephemeral NVMe disks facilitates high-throughput data processing. The local NVMe capacity removes network storage latency dependencies for intermediate computation phases.

Cost efficiency is centered around dense hardware consolidation. By delivering substantial memory footprints alongside 11.4 TB of high-speed local disk and high-bandwidth networking in a single physical host, the server reduces the necessity of managing distributed nodes for large dataset tasks. However, instance store volumes are ephemeral, requiring external data replication or persistent storage layers to mitigate data loss risks on hardware termination.

The r8idb.metal-48xl is primarily suited for large-scale in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching clusters, big data processing pipelines, and high-performance transactional database workloads requiring direct bare-metal hardware access.
